name: Complex
analyticAt_iff_eventually_differentiableAt
result.signature: {f : ℂ → E} {c : ℂ} : AnalyticAt ℂ f c ↔ ∀ᶠ z in 𝓝 c, DifferentiableAt ℂ f z
result.type:
∀ {E : Type u} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℂ E] [CompleteSpace E] {f : ℂ → E} {c : ℂ},
  AnalyticAt ℂ f c ↔ ∀ᶠ (z : ℂ) in nhds c, DifferentiableAt ℂ f z
result.value:
:= by
  constructor
  · intro fa
    filter_upwards [fa.eventually_analyticAt]
    apply AnalyticAt.differentiableAt
  · intro d
    rcases _root_.eventually_nhds_iff.mp d with ⟨s, d, o, m⟩
    have h : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ f s := by
      refine DifferentiableOn.analyticOnNhd ?_ o
      intro z m
      exact (d z m).differentiableWithinAt
    exact h _ m
result.informal_name: Analyticity at a Point iff Eventual Differentiability in Complex Plane
result.informal_description: A function $ f: \mathbb{C} \to E $ is analytic at a point $ c \in \mathbb{C} $ if and only if there exists a neighborhood of $ c $ where $ f $ is complex differentiable at every point in that neighborhood.

name: AnalyticAt
differentiableAt
result.signature: : AnalyticAt 𝕜 f x → DifferentiableAt 𝕜 f x
result.informal_name: Analyticity Implies Differentiability at a Point
result.informal_description: If a function $ f $ is analytic at a point $ x $, then it is differentiable at $ x $. This means that the existence of a formal power series expansion of $ f $ around $ x $ with positive radius of convergence guarantees the existence of the Fréchet derivative of $ f $ at $ x $.

name: AnalyticOn
differentiableOn
result.signature: (h : AnalyticOn 𝕜 f s) : DifferentiableOn 𝕜 f s
result.value: := fun y hy ↦ (h y hy).differentiableWithinAt.mono (by simp)
result.informal_name: Analyticity Implies Differentiability on the Set
result.informal_description: If a function $ f $ is analytic on a set $ S $ with respect to a nontrivially normed field $ \mathbb{K} $, then $ f $ is differentiable on $ S $.

name: eventually_closedBall_subset
result.signature: {x : α} {u : Set α} (hu : u ∈ 𝓝 x) : ∀ᶠ r in 𝓝 (0 : ℝ), closedBall x r ⊆ u
result.type:
∀ {α : Type u_2} [inst : PseudoMetricSpace α] {x : α} {u : Set α},
  u ∈ nhds x → ∀ᶠ (r : ℝ) in nhds 0, Metric.closedBall x r ⊆ u
result.value:
:= by
  obtain ⟨ε, εpos, hε⟩ : ∃ ε, 0 < ε ∧ closedBall x ε ⊆ u := nhds_basis_closedBall.mem_iff.1 hu
  have : Iic ε ∈ 𝓝 (0 : ℝ) := Iic_mem_nhds εpos
  filter_upwards [this] with _ hr using Subset.trans (closedBall_subset_closedBall hr) hε
result.informal_name: Closed Balls Eventually Contained in Neighborhoods in Pseudo-Metric Spaces
result.informal_description: For any neighborhood $ u $ of a point $ x $ in a pseudo-metric space $ \alpha $, there exists a neighborhood $ V $ of $ 0 $ in $ \mathbb{R} $ such that for all $ r \in V $, the closed ball $ \overline{B}(x, r) $ is contained in $ u $. Equivalently, for any neighborhood $ u $ of $ x $, there exists $ \delta > 0 $ such that $ \overline{B}_r(x) \subseteq u $ for all $ 0 < r < \delta $.

name: EMetric
closedBall_mem_nhds
result.signature: (x : α) {ε : ℝ≥0∞} (ε0 : 0 < ε) : closedBall x ε ∈ 𝓝 x
result.type: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : PseudoEMetricSpace α] (x : α) {ε : ENNReal}, 0 < ε → EMetric.closedBall x ε ∈ nhds x
result.informal_name: Closed Ball with Positive Radius is a Neighborhood in Pseudo Extended Metric Space
result.informal_description: In a pseudo extended metric space, for any point $ x $ and positive radius $ \varepsilon $, the closed ball centered at $ x $ with radius $ \varepsilon $ (defined as $ \{ y \in \alpha \mid \text{edist}(y, x) \leq \varepsilon \} $) is a neighborhood of $ x $, i.e., it belongs to the neighborhood filter $ \mathsf{nhds}(x) $.

name: Metric
nhds_basis_closedBall
result.type: ∀ {α : Type u} [inst : PseudoMetricSpace α] {x : α}, (nhds x).HasBasis (fun ε => 0 < ε) (Metric.closedBall x)
result.informal_name: Neighborhood Filter Basis: Closed Balls in Pseudo-Metric Space
result.informal_description: In a pseudo-metric space, the neighborhood filter at a point $x$ has a basis consisting of closed balls centered at $x$ with positive radii $\varepsilon > 0$. This means that for every neighborhood of $x$, there exists a closed ball $\{y \mid d(x, y) \leq \varepsilon\}$ contained within it.
